html:
At Las Navas de Tolosa in the Sierra Morena, on 16 July 1212, the united armies of Castile, Aragon and Navarre defeated the Almohad caliph Muhammad al-Nasir.

The Almohads, a Berber dynasty from Morocco, ruled al-Andalus and had beaten Castile in 1195. The pope declared a crusade, and the Christian kings joined forces. A shepherd is said to have shown them a hidden pass through the mountains, and they routed the caliph's army.

Almohad power in Spain collapsed. Within forty years Castile took Córdoba and Seville, and Aragon took Valencia and the Balearic islands. Only the small kingdom of Granada remained Muslim, until the Granada War of 1492. It was the turning point of the Reconquista. See Spain.
sum: At Las Navas de Tolosa in the Sierra Morena, on 16 July 1212, the united armies of Castile, Aragon and Navarre defeated the Almohad caliph Muhammad al-Nasir.
